body:
Four tests in tests/unit/test_1596_module_entry_point.py fail on a plain
developer checkout:

    python -P -m cps --help
    -> No module named cps

They run the interpreter with -P from an arbitrary cwd, which is the point of
the test (the s6 longrun does exactly that with cwd=/config), but it also means
PYTHONPATH=. cannot help and the package must actually be installed into the
environment. CI installs it, so CI is green and the gap is invisible there;
repo/.venv does not, so anyone running the unit suite locally sees four red
tests unrelated to their change.

Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to any branch: reproduced on clean main by
stashing (4 failed, 14 passed).

Cost is small but real: it trains local runs to ignore red, which is how a
genuine failure gets waved through. Either skip with a clear reason when
importlib.util.find_spec("cps") is None outside an install, or have the test
create the editable install it needs.

Found while running blast-radius checks for #1110.
title: test_1596_module_entry_point silently requires an editable install
